uncited: A GPU-based algorithm to voxelize solid geometry in a single pass, producing point-sampled or over/under-conservative results.
It differs from boundary-only voxelization by producing a fully filled interior volume and from multi-pass methods by extracting up to 1024 layers in a single geometry pass.
Unlike [8, 10], it is accurate even if an arbitrary number of fragments fall in a single voxel and does not require front/back face separation.
**Inputs:** A watertight mesh (manifold or topologically coherent mesh not required).
**Outputs:** A 3D voxel grid representing the solid interior.
In DX10, this supports multiple render targets (MRT).
*   **Voxel Column:** A 32-bit integer (or bitset) representing occupancy for a column of voxels.
**Rasterization:** Render the input mesh to the slicemap.
Each fragment contributes to the voxel column corresponding to its screen-space position.
**Bitmask Accumulation:** Accumulate fragment bitmasks using bitwise XOR.
This exploits the Jordan curve theorem: a point is interior if a ray from it intersects the surface an odd number of times.
**Symmetric Difference:** For intersecting watertight models, the algorithm computes the symmetric difference (hollow representation), not the union.
This is consistent with the definition of watertight surfaces.
**Density Computation:** Compute density using a kernel of size $2^3$.
This is fast and memory efficient because all information is tightly packed.
*   **Maximum layers per pass without MRT on DX9:** 32.
*   **DX9 without MRT:** Performance converges to ~23x speedup over [5] rather than 4x, possibly due to G6 MRT sweet spot.
*   **DX9 Implementation:** Treats all four color components equally, reflecting vector capacities of older processors.
It would not scale for DX10 hardware because a lookup texture for a 32-bit integer would need $2^{32}$ entries and not fit into GPU memory.
Accurate even if arbitrary fragments fall in a single voxel.
Does not require front/back face separation.
Simple models (low geometric complexity, high fill-rate) are worst-case scenarios because standard rendering is very cheap.
*   When high-speed voxelization of complex watertight models is required.
*   When MRT support is available (DX10) or when older cards without MRT are used (DX9).
*   When union of intersecting models is required (algorithm computes symmetric difference).
*   When manifold or topologically coherent mesh is not available (watertight input suffices, but non-watertight may produce unexpected results).
The approach is simple but efficient single-pass solutions were previously non-existent.
It is appealing due to its accuracy and simplicity.
